help: The Model Lab builds a physics model the way a researcher would, without being walked through it: it chooses the equations, fetches the data, builds and runs the model, proves it is solved correctly against analytic solutions and conservation laws, calibrates on part of the record, tests on part it never saw, finds which assumption matters most, and writes the methods and results. It says plainly whether the result is only verified, or also calibrated and validated, and for a hazard it has no verified solver for it researches the physics and data and tells you what is missing instead of guessing. It covers flood inundation, air quality, extreme heat, extreme rainfall, extreme wind, fire weather, drought, river flow, tropical cyclone wind, earthquake shaking, landslide susceptibility. Say, for example: "build a flood model for Chattogram", "earthquake hazard for Tokyo" or "air quality model for Delhi".
